I have strong evidence. Key facts:

1. Repeatable Read in PG prevents phantoms (stronger than SQL standard minimum), but serialization anomalies are still possible; "Attempts to enforce business rules by transactions running at this isolation level are not likely to work correctly without careful use of explicit locks" (transaction-iso.html#XACT-REPEATABLE-READ). So proposal's premise that RR + no phantoms = serial equivalence is wrong.

2. Retry unit must be the whole transaction, including the application logic that decides which SQL to issue. "It is important to retry the complete transaction, including all logic that decides which SQL to issue and/or which values to use. Therefore, PostgreSQL does not offer an automatic retry facility." (mvcc-serialization-failure-handling.html). Also transaction-iso.html#XACT-REPEATABLE-READ: "When an application receives this error message, it should abort the current transaction and retry the whole transaction from the beginning."

3. Ownership of retry: application/framework, not server. applevel-consistency.html#SERIALIZABLE-CONSISTENCY: "it will avoid creating an unnecessary burden for application programmers if the application software goes through a framework which automatically retries transactions which are rolled back with a serialization failure."

4. Unique violations (23505): only retry in some cases, with care, because they might represent persistent error conditions rather than transient failures (mvcc-serialization-failure-handling.html). So unconditional retry bucket is wrong. Also note the serializable corner case of unique constraint violations after checking key absence (transaction-iso.html#XACT-SERIALIZABLE).

5. Three-attempt bound under contention: not documentable. "Transaction retry does not guarantee that the retried transaction will complete; multiple retries may be needed. In cases with very high contention, it is possible that completion of a transaction may take many attempts. In cases involving a conflicting prepared transaction, it may not be possible to make progress until the prepared transaction commits or rolls back." — so no such promise can be made. UNVERIFIED/unsupported.

6. Recommendation: use Serializable for the read-then-write different-rows invariant, since RR doesn't detect the read/write dependency cycle; alternatively keep RR with explicit locks (SELECT FOR UPDATE / LOCK TABLE). Also mention deadlock retries 40P01, and SQLSTATE-based classification (40001, 40P01, 23505, 23P01) — errcodes-appendix. Also note: "only updating transactions might need to be retried; read-only transactions will never have serialization conflicts."

7. Also useful: SERIALIZABLE READ ONLY DEFERRABLE for read-only consistency (transaction-iso #XACT-SERIALIZABLE).
